idea.title: Mitigating Medium Novelty Bias in Multi-Agent Scientific Ideation via Latent Probing
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent scientific ideation frameworks overcome systematic biases in novelty judgment to generate truly high-impact research directions?
idea.research_gap: While recent frameworks generate literature-grounded scientific ideas and assess novelty using retrieval and multi-agent dialogue, language models suffer from a pervasive "medium novelty" bias where their final judgments and iterative refinements diverge from human gold standards due to miscalibrated reasoning-to-judgment translation.
idea.methodology: We propose a unified pipeline combining multi-agent ideation with a latent-probing calibration mechanism. During the generation and critique loop, where generator and critic agents iteratively refine research directions, we integrate a Think-Probe-Respond layer. Instead of allowing the model's final text generation to default to safe, medium-novelty compromises, we probe the hidden states during the critique phase to extract latent novelty judgments. These probed signals condition the final refinement prompt, steering the multi-agent system toward genuinely novel conceptual spaces.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated multi-agent scientific ideation framework that leverages latent probing to eliminate medium-novelty bias, yielding research directions with higher technical depth and verified novelty scores.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize the RINoBench benchmark and the SciMON generation task setup. We deploy a multi-agent ideation architecture consisting of diverse personas (generator, reviewer, domain expert) using frozen LLM APIs. We compare our latent-probe-enhanced multi-agent loop against standard multi-agent generation baselines and standalone SciMON configurations across 200 standard computer science research background contexts.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate the generated ideas using RINoBench metrics and the Idea Novelty Checker framework. We measure alignment with human expert novelty judgments, distribution variance across novelty tiers to verify mitigation of the medium-novelty bias, and technical depth scores.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to standard LLM APIs for multi-agent generation and hidden state extraction.
Availability of the public RINoBench dataset for evaluation.
Feasibility of completing the 6-week project timeline without model weight training.

idea.title: Integrating Automated Novelty Assessment into Chain-of-Ideas Scientific Generation
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent literature-grounded research ideation systems automatically prevent incremental or redundant proposals without manual intervention?
idea.research_gap: While recent frameworks like Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) and ResearchAgent generate structured research proposals using iterative review loops, they lack a dedicated, automated novelty verification mechanism during the generation trajectory. Conversely, novelty checkers operate entirely post-hoc rather than guiding generation interactively.
idea.methodology: We propose a modular pipeline combining Chain-of-Ideas generation with a facet-based retrieval-augmented novelty checker. During each intermediate step of idea refinement, the system queries a scientific literature index, extracts core facets using an LLM, and computes a dynamic novelty score. If the novelty score falls below a threshold, the feedback loop prompts the generator agent to pivot its conceptual trajectory away from existing prior art.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated, automated ideation framework that demonstrably increases the novelty and technical depth of generated research proposals while maintaining high logical consistency and feasibility.
idea.experimental_setup: We select a benchmark set of 100 recent computer science and NLP papers published across top-tier venues. We initialize our generation agents using seed papers from past years and task the system with proposing follow-up directions. We compare our integrated novelty-guided CoI approach against baseline vanilla CoI and ResearchAgent configurations.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate the generated ideas using both automated LLM-as-a-judge protocols (Idea Arena style preferences) and manual expert assessment on dimensions of novelty, technical depth, feasibility, and clarity on a 5-point Likert scale.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to API-based LLMs for multi-agent generation and facet extraction.
Availability of public pre-computed embeddings and vector databases for scientific literature retrieval.
Execution timeline fits within a 6-week university project window using existing open-source frameworks.

idea.title: Mitigating Medium Novelty Bias in Multi-Agent Scientific Ideation via Latent Probing and Prompt Conditioning
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent scientific ideation frameworks overcome systematic medium-novelty biases in model reasoning to generate truly high-impact research directions?
idea.research_gap: While recent frameworks generate literature-grounded scientific ideas and assess novelty using retrieval and multi-agent dialogue, language models suffer from a pervasive medium novelty bias where their final judgments and iterative refinements diverge from human gold standards. Existing work like Think-Probe-Respond addresses this bias exclusively as a single-model evaluation task rather than an active multi-agent generation and steering mechanism, and lacks integration with iterative generation loops like SciMON.
idea.methodology: We propose an integrated multi-agent ideation pipeline incorporating latent-probe-based prompt conditioning. To adhere to hardware limits of a single 12GB consumer GPU within a 6-week timeline, we use locally hosted open-weights 4-bit quantized Llama-3-8B-Instruct models without full fine-tuning. Instead of unstable live runtime activation vector manipulation, we extract hidden states from the critic agent during its reasoning phase and apply offline-trained lightweight linear probes to predict explicit novelty tiers. The continuous probed novelty scores are mapped via a discrete translation function into natural prompt prefixes injected into the generator agent's context, pulling outputs away from safe medium-novelty compromises toward high-risk, high-reward conceptual spaces.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated multi-agent scientific ideation framework leveraging open-weights hidden state probing and lightweight prompt-level conditioning to eliminate medium-novelty bias, yielding research directions with higher technical depth and verified novelty scores without requiring full LLM fine-tuning.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize a representative subset of 50 background contexts drawn from the RINoBench benchmark and SciMON generation tasks to ensure compute feasibility. We deploy a multi-agent ideation architecture consisting of diverse personas (generator, reviewer, domain expert) using locally hosted Llama-3-8B-Instruct models. We compare our probe-enhanced multi-agent loop against standard multi-agent generation baselines, standalone SciMON configurations, a prompt-only novelty constraint text baseline, and classifier-guided decoding baselines.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated ideas using RINoBench metrics and the Idea Novelty Checker framework. We measure alignment with human expert novelty judgments, distribution variance across novelty tiers to verify mitigation of medium-novelty bias, technical depth scores, and computational footprint analysis tracking latency and memory overhead on the consumer GPU. We also include a falsification baseline to verify whether prompt conditioning yields actual technical depth rather than superficial lexical novelty.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to locally hosted open-weights models (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) compatible with a 12GB consumer GPU via 4-bit quantization.
Availability of public RINoBench dataset and SciMON benchmark contexts for evaluation.
Feasibility of completing the 6-week project timeline using frozen base weights and offline-trained lightweight linear probes without full LLM fine-tuning.
Reliance on discrete prompt conditioning derived from a robust fallback mapping function to maintain semantic coherence and avoid VRAM bottlenecks.

idea.title: Integrating Automated Novelty Assessment into Milestone-Gated Chain-of-Ideas Scientific Generation
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent literature-grounded research ideation systems automatically prevent incremental or redundant proposals without inducing degenerate lexical avoidance, excessive API latency, or unfeasible conceptual drift?
idea.research_gap: While frameworks like Chain-of-Ideas and ResearchAgent generate structured research proposals using iterative review loops, they lack a dedicated, automated novelty verification mechanism during generation trajectories. Prior novelty-checking approaches operate post-hoc or run heavy retrieval-rerank loops at every step, creating severe latency, high API costs, and perverse incentives for the generator to make unfeasible adjustments to clear arbitrary thresholds. Furthermore, existing work does not combine dynamic uncertainty-driven milestone scheduling with soft penalty-based optimization to guarantee logical soundness without trapping agents in trivial local optima.
idea.methodology: We propose an ideation pipeline combining Chain-of-Ideas generation with a facet-based retrieval-augmented novelty checker and a soft penalty-based feasibility rule. Instead of static milestone gating or continuous step-by-step loops, novelty checks and feedback loops are triggered dynamically via an uncertainty-driven adaptive trigger based on entropy over the generator's token distribution or semantic variance across intermediate steps. At these adaptive checkpoints, the system queries a pre-computed vector database of scientific literature, extracts core facets using an LLM, and computes a dynamic novelty score. Crucially, rather than using a hard binary filter that causes objective conflict, the programmatic feasibility check is formulated as a soft penalty within the reward model. Conflicting feedback signals between novelty and feasibility are reconciled using a weighted preference-alignment function that prevents the pruning of unconventional yet valid paradigms.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated, cost-efficient ideation framework that increases the technical depth and novelty of generated research proposals while preserving logical consistency and experimental feasibility, accompanied by a formal ablation study detailing the latency-novelty trade-off curve and sensitivity analysis on milestone granularity.
idea.experimental_setup: We select a benchmark subset of 25 recent computer science and NLP papers published across top-tier venues to fit practical API budgets. We initialize our generation agents using seed papers from past years and task the system with proposing follow-up directions. We leverage existing open-source implementations of ResearchAgent, SciMON, and vanilla Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) to serve as baselines, and compare our uncertainty-driven adaptive novelty-guided CoI approach against them.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated ideas using automated LLM-as-a-judge protocols (Idea Arena style preferences), manual expert assessment on dimensions of novelty, technical depth, feasibility, and clarity on a 5-point Likert scale, and a historical prediction benchmark tasking the system with generating follow-up papers from a historical cutoff year to check overlap with actually published breakthroughs. We also conduct an explicit ablation study comparing the latency, cost, and novelty trade-off of adaptive uncertainty-driven gating versus static milestone spacing and continuous step-by-step checking.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to API-based LLMs for multi-agent generation and facet extraction.
Availability of public pre-computed embeddings and vector databases (such as Semantic Scholar snapshots) for scientific literature retrieval.

Execution timeline fits within a 6-week university project window using open-source agent frameworks (such as pre-existing implementations of ResearchAgent and SciMON) and local quantized language models for intermediate steps combined with targeted API calls for final evaluation.

To resolve cascading distribution shifts and hardware bottlenecks, linear probes are pre-computed and frozen offline using a static validation set rather than dynamically trained online. During the critic phase, hidden-state activations of the model evaluating an idea are extracted via these frozen probes to surface underlying novelty tiers (low, medium, high). These continuous probe outputs are mapped into soft, continuous prompt conditioning scalars to condition subsequent generator refinement prompts to break the medium-novelty compromise loop. We explicitly incorporate a lightweight validation phase to test probe calibration on intermediate generation outputs and employ activation caching and 4-bit quantization under a concrete memory and throughput profiling protocol.

We deploy a multi-agent ideation architecture (generator, critic, domain expert) using open-weight Llama-3 models locally within a 12GB VRAM constraint utilizing activation caching and 4-bit quantization. idea.title: Topological Idea-Evolution and Milestone Synchronization in Multi-Agent Research Ideation
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent literature-grounded research ideation systems automatically prevent incremental or redundant proposals without incurring the computational overhead of continuous per-step retrieval or the high overlap of isolated, post-hoc novelty checkers?
idea.research_gap: While frameworks like Chain-of-Ideas (2025.findings-emnlp.477) generate structured research proposals using iterative review loops, they lack a dedicated, automated verification mechanism embedded directly during the generation trajectory. Existing approaches either rely on costly continuous per-step retrieval (causing latency and generation stagnation) or function as post-hoc filters (2025.sdp-1.9). Moreover, previous iterative systems (2024.acl-long.18) lack topological idea-evolution structures and fail to integrate explicit multi-agent critique diversity or rigorous constraint filtering, often causing LLMs to pivot into infeasible technical spaces just to clear arbitrary novelty thresholds. Furthermore, prior work leaves unaddressed whether simple prompt-engineered loops with static penalties achieve identical novelty without structural milestones.
idea.methodology: We propose a modular multi-agent pipeline combining Chain-of-Ideas (2025.findings-emnlp.477) generation with a milestone-synchronized, facet-based retrieval-augmented novelty checker (2025.sdp-1.9) and a hard-constraint feasibility filter. We formalize 'milestones' as discrete structural transition checkpoints (e.g., transition from problem formulation to method design) to prevent arbitrary triggering. At each milestone, the system queries a scientific literature index, extracts core facets using an LLM, and computes a dynamic novelty score via an adaptive thresholding mechanism. To prevent infinite retry loops and semantic drift, any conceptual trajectory pivot enforced by the novelty feedback loop must pass a streamlined, single-pass multi-agent critic panel evaluating technical feasibility and logical coherence asynchronously, mitigating compounding hallucinations.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated, automated ideation framework that increases the novelty and technical depth of generated research proposals while maintaining high logical consistency, controlling API token costs, avoiding generation stagnation, and incorporating domain-specific feasibility constraints.
idea.experimental_setup: We select a benchmark set of 100 recent computer science and NLP papers published across top-tier venues. We initialize our generation agents using seed papers from past years and task the system with proposing follow-up directions. We compare our integrated milestone-based novelty-guided CoI approach against baseline vanilla CoI (2025.findings-emnlp.477), ResearchAgent (2025.naacl-long.342), continuous per-step RAG configurations, and a control baseline where the novelty checker is completely decoupled from the generation loop to isolate the effect of synchronous interruption.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated proposals using a dual protocol: (1) automated evaluation metrics and benchmarks including RINoBench (2026.lrec-1.370) and Idea Arena (2026.emnlp-main.688) soft-accuracy configurations, and (2) manual expert assessment on dimensions of novelty, technical depth, feasibility, and clarity on a 5-point Likert scale, alongside a wall-clock execution time and token cost analysis.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to API-based LLMs for multi-agent generation and facet extraction.
Availability of public pre-computed embeddings and vector databases for scientific literature retrieval.
Execution timeline fits within a 6-week university project window using existing open-source frameworks and focusing evaluation on a narrowed subset of papers.

idea.title: Mitigating Medium Novelty Bias in Multi-Agent Scientific Ideation via In-Context Reflection and Contrastive Critique
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent scientific ideation frameworks overcome systematic biases in novelty judgment to generate truly high-impact research directions without relying on inaccessible internal model states?
idea.research_gap: While recent frameworks generate literature-grounded scientific ideas and assess novelty using retrieval and multi-agent dialogue, language models suffer from a pervasive medium novelty bias where final judgments and iterative refinements diverge from human gold standards. Existing mitigation methods like Think-Probe-Respond require internal hidden-state access which is infeasible with commercial APIs, and purely textual multi-agent prompts fail to structurally correct this miscalibration.
idea.methodology: We propose a unified pipeline combining multi-agent ideation with an explicit in-context reflection and contrastive critique mechanism. Rather than relying on hidden-state probing, which is incompatible with black-box APIs, or incurring massive computational overhead, our framework inserts an explicit chain-of-thought novelty classification phase during the critic agent's loop. The critic agent categorizes intermediate ideas into explicit novelty tiers based on reference literature retrieved via the Idea Novelty Checker framework, followed by a contrastive prompt conditioning step. To ensure prompt-based steering avoids superficial text transformations, we implement a dynamic debate protocol where generator agents must explicitly address and refute specific overlapping baseline papers identified by the critic before revising their proposals. We also provide strict fallback parsing logic for multi-agent outputs to handle cases where LLM critic agents fail to strictly format novelty tier categorizations.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated multi-agent scientific ideation framework leveraging black-box compatible in-context reflection and contrastive critique to eliminate medium-novelty bias, yielding research directions with higher technical depth and verified novelty scores.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize the RINoBench benchmark and the SciMON generation task setup. We deploy a multi-agent ideation architecture consisting of diverse personas using standard commercial LLM APIs. To manage API latency and cumulative financial costs, we reduce our evaluation subset to a representative sample of 25 computer science research background contexts for pipeline tuning and evaluation. We implement token usage limits, local caching mechanisms for retrieval results, and asynchronous API calls to minimize execution time and cost.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate the generated ideas using RINoBench metrics and the Idea Novelty Checker framework. We measure alignment with human expert novelty judgments, distribution variance across novelty tiers to verify mitigation of the medium-novelty bias, and technical depth scores. We incorporate controlled ablation studies comparing text-only in-context contrastive prompting directly against standard multi-agent reviewer-generator revision loops to isolate the impact of our contrastive structuring.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to standard commercial LLM APIs for multi-agent generation and critique loops.
Availability of the public RINoBench dataset and Idea Novelty Checker framework for evaluation.
Feasibility of completing the 6-week project timeline using API-based execution without local hidden-state extraction or model weight training.

idea.title: Mitigating Medium Novelty Bias in Multi-Agent Scientific Ideation via Latent Probing
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent scientific ideation frameworks overcome systematic biases in novelty judgment to generate truly high-impact research directions?
idea.research_gap: While recent frameworks generate literature-grounded scientific ideas and assess novelty using retrieval and multi-agent dialogue, language models suffer from a pervasive medium novelty bias where their final judgments and iterative refinements diverge from human gold standards due to miscalibrated reasoning-to-judgment translation.
idea.methodology: To resolve the trade-off between white-box access required for hidden state extraction and practical API constraints on a single 12GB consumer GPU, we restrict our architecture to open-source models (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) using 4-bit quantization and activation checkpointing to avoid memory bottlenecks. We integrate a Think-Probe-Respond layer into the multi-agent critique loop, augmented by a preliminary probe training phase on a validation split of RINoBench to verify that hidden states linearly separate novelty tiers prior to integration. During generation and critique, we probe hidden states to extract latent novelty judgments instead of relying on default text output. We define a programmatic mapping function where the probed continuous latent vector is transformed via a linear projection layer into a soft prompt prefix. To address semantic mismatch and prevent collapse, we include explicit monitoring of semantic drift and KL divergence against base generation distributions during the prompt-prefix conditioning step, steering the multi-agent system toward genuinely novel conceptual spaces without compromising textual coherence.
idea.expected_contribution: An integrated open-source multi-agent scientific ideation framework that leverages latent probing with explicit memory optimization and semantic drift monitoring to eliminate medium-novelty bias, yielding research directions with higher technical depth and verified novelty scores while preserving overall textual coherence.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize the RINoBench benchmark and the SciMON generation task setup. We deploy a multi-agent ideation architecture consisting of diverse personas (generator, reviewer, domain expert) using Llama-3-8B-Instruct on a single 12 GB consumer GPU with 4-bit quantization. We compare our latent-probe-enhanced multi-agent loop against standard multi-agent generation baselines and standalone SciMON configurations across 200 standard computer science research background contexts. We include an explicit validation step measuring generation perplexity and coherence scores to confirm that conditioning the final prompt with probed latent signals does not degrade technical depth or text quality.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated ideas using RINoBench metrics and the Idea Novelty Checker framework. We measure alignment with human expert novelty judgments, distribution variance across novelty tiers to verify mitigation of medium-novelty bias, generation perplexity for textual coherence, and a small-scale human expert evaluation subset to validate whether reduced medium-novelty bias translates to genuinely valuable and feasible scientific ideas.
feasibility_assumptions: Availability of open-source model weights (e.g., Llama-3-8B-Instruct) for hidden state extraction on a single 12 GB consumer GPU using 4-bit quantization and activation checkpointing.
Availability of the public RINoBench dataset and SciMON benchmark contexts for evaluation.

Feasibility of completing the 6-week project timeline without full model weight training, restricting intervention to inference-time latent probing, linear projection mapping, and prompt conditioning.
